description:
On the /fly route, the left-rail HUD panel's velocity readout displays 'NaN km/s' for the entire duration of outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres). The same readout shows correct values (e.g. ~29.78 km/s) for Earth, Moon, and Mars missions

Expected: The HUD velocity readout should show a finite numeric spacecraft speed (km/s) computed correctly for the mission's actual transfer orbit at its current heliocentric distance

Acceptance criteria:
- A Galileo mission (Jupiter, ~2242-day transit) at any point during cruise shows a finite number > 0 km/s, not NaN [reporter: 'Flying out to the outer planets, the HUD speed readout just says "NaN km/s" the whole way']
- A Voyager 2 mission (Neptune, ~4388-day transit) at any point during cruise shows a finite number > 0 km/s, not NaN [reporter: same report — 'outer planets' includes Neptune]
- A Cassini mission (Saturn) at any point during its cruise shows a finite number > 0 km/s, not NaN [reporter: same report — 'outer planets' includes Saturn]
- The ORRERY-1 default Mars free-return scenario still shows ~32.7 km/s at Earth departure (r=1.0 AU on the Earth-Mars Hohmann) — existing Earth/Mars behavior is not regressed [spec: static/data/scenarios/orrery-1.json is the default fly scenario; unit test at fly-physics.test.ts:32-34 expects heliocentricSpeed(1.0, 1.262) ≈ 32.73 km/s]
- Moon-mode missions (isMoonMission=true) still show ~29.78 km/s — the R_EARTH_AU branch for both arguments (line 952) remains valid [code-invariant: src/routes/fly/+page.svelte lines 950-953: isMoonMission passes R_EARTH_AU as both r and a, which is always in the valid domain]
